brief.name: Dext
brief.summary: Dext is a Visual Studio Code extension for AI conversations, delegated code changes, plan execution, and reusable typed workflows. It also provides conversation history, development reviews, long-term project knowledge, and independently configured inline completion.
goals: Help developers understand code and delegate implementation work.
Execute implementation plans with progress tracking and a separate final verification.
Turn repeated tasks into reusable workflows using APIs, Skills, and MCP tools.
Keep development reviews connected to their execution while maintaining reusable project knowledge.
Provide inline completion using bounded project context and optional local adaptation.
runtime: Codex CLI, Claude CLI, or DeepSeek Harness for AI tasks, using the selected CLI's credentials.
Dext parses and validates a subset of Python syntax without requiring a Python interpreter.
Optional API Key models or local Ollama for inline completion.
audiences: Developers working in Visual Studio Code.

capabilities.description: Offer read-only code understanding through Ask and implementation work through Agent, with files and selections supplied as context.
outcomes: Questions about code can be explored without changing files.
Features, fixes, and checks can be delegated to an Agent.

evidence.note: Ask understands code without changing files.
Agent implements features, fixes bugs, and runs checks.
Files and selections can be added as context.

capabilities.description: Create and revise an implementation plan, then execute it through Build with repeated progress assessment and separate final verification.
outcomes: Unfinished actionable tasks continue across execution rounds.
Matching task progress can be restored when Build is invoked again for the same plan.
Execution distinguishes Completed, Stopped, Blocked, and Incomplete outcomes.

capabilities.description: Compose API calls in Code mode using Dext's Python subset, with completion, parameter hints, type checking, and reusable project APIs.
outcomes: Repeated tasks can be expressed through APIs, Skills, and MCP tools.
Custom APIs can be saved as .dx files under .dext/api/.
API diagnostics identify compilation problems.

capabilities.description: Revisit conversations in History and record a conversation as an editable starting workflow.
outcomes: Previous conversations remain available for reuse.
A conversation can become a starting point for workflow automation.

capabilities.description: Present changed files, recorded script facts and coverage, knowledge drafts, and an accept or request-changes decision in the conversation.
outcomes: Review decisions remain associated with a particular execution.

capabilities.description: Maintain Overview, Knowledge, and Diagrams in Project, including individual knowledge drafts that a developer chooses to adopt.
outcomes: Project information remains separate from single-run records.
Adopting a draft writes one long-term object and opens it in Project.

capabilities.description: Provide source-code suggestions through a separately configured completion model, using bounded context and optional local weak-feedback adaptation.
outcomes: Suggestions support single-line identifier replacement and bounded multi-line insertion.
Completion can use nearby text, background definitions, recent edits, and relevant saved-code references.
Developers can select adaptation modes and clear project completion memory.

evidence.uncertainty: The documentation does not establish a verified improvement in real-model quality from persistent adaptation.

flows.description: Build executes a selected plan, assesses and checkpoints successive rounds, and requires separate final verification before Completed. Cancellation, comprehensive external blocking, stagnation, and the execution ceiling produce distinct non-completion outcomes.
flows.trigger: The developer selects a final plan and clicks Build in Plan mode.

steps.label: Select the final implementation plan and click Build.

evidence.note: Another Build restores matching tasks from the same plan.

steps.label: Execute a round, check reported progress, and save a checkpoint; continue while unfinished work is actionable and no stopping condition applies.
When every task is reported complete, request separate Agent inspection of the implementation and checks.

evidence.uncertainty: The excerpt does not specify the full retry or failure routing for unsuccessful final verification.

steps.label: Display Completed after final verification passes.
Display Stopped when the user cancels.
Display Blocked when explicit external blockers cover every remaining task.
Display Incomplete and preserve the plan after three rounds without new completed tasks or new tool activity, or at the 64-round ceiling.

outcomes: Completed requires a separate final verification.
Stopped, Blocked, and Incomplete distinguish documented stopping conditions.
Round checkpoints preserve progress without changing the plan document.

terms.definition: The natural-language mode for understanding code and exploring questions without changing files.
The natural-language mode for implementing features, fixing bugs, and running checks. The documentation also uses Agent for the selected AI executor.
The mode for creating and revising an implementation plan; a selected final plan can subsequently be executed with Build.
The action that executes a selected implementation plan in Plan mode. A later Build can restore matching task progress from the same plan.
The mode for composing and running typed API workflows using Dext's supported subset of Python syntax.
A callable operation in a typed workflow. Built-ins include ask, print, and terminal; reusable custom project APIs are stored in .dx files under .dext/api/.
A collapsible conversation record of development changes, recorded script facts and coverage, knowledge drafts, and the developer's review decision, scoped to a particular execution.
A proposed knowledge item surfaced in Review that can be independently adopted as one long-term object in Project.
Plan execution progress saved in conversation history after rounds, without editing the plan document, supporting restoration of matching tasks on a later Build.
Completion experience behavior selected through off, session, or workspace mode. Session is the initial default; workspace persists local weak-feedback statistics and validated references.

constraints.statement: Ask remains read-only and produces no acceptance card; writing a Plan produces no implementation Review.
constraints.rationale: The documented review boundary distinguishes understanding and planning from implementation work.

constraints.statement: Project APIs require a trusted workspace.
constraints.rationale: Workspace trust is an explicit prerequisite for project API use.

constraints.statement: A normal Agent return or completed task reports do not establish Plan completion; Completed requires separate final verification.
constraints.rationale: Final verification relies on Agent inspection of the implementation and checks. Task reports alone cannot independently prove correctness.

constraints.statement: Review acceptance belongs to sessionId + turnId + runId and is not inherited by retries or later Builds. Plan reviews additionally bind the plan content version and Build run.
constraints.rationale: The documented identity prevents a different execution from carrying an earlier acceptance.

constraints.statement: Accepting code Review and adopting a knowledge draft are independent actions; adopting one draft writes one long-term object.
constraints.rationale: Code acceptance does not itself adopt proposed project knowledge.

constraints.statement: Completion source snippets follow workspace boundaries, .dextignore, and the configured .gitignore policy. Workspace adaptation stores local statistics and validated references, not raw code copies or feedback logs sent to a training service.
constraints.rationale: The documented completion contract bounds both source context and persistent experience.

decisions.title: Dext owns its supported workflow language
decisions.decision: Workflows use a small Python syntax subset parsed and validated by Dext, with supported expressions and helpers compiled by Dext.
consequences: A Python interpreter is not required.
API parameters and result fields support completion and type checking.

decisions.title: Project content and execution Review have separate responsibilities
decisions.decision: Project contains long-term Overview, Knowledge, and Diagrams, while execution evidence and review decisions remain in the conversation.
consequences: Project excludes Hook logs, task checklists, and single-run records.
Knowledge drafts enter Project through individual adoption.

decisions.title: Persistent completion adaptation remains opt-in
decisions.decision: Use session as the initial adaptation default and retain workspace persistence as an explicit option pending held-out quality and latency comparisons.
consequences: Persistent cross-session completion experience is not initially enabled.
The documented default is conditional on future quality and latency evidence.
